intro: Arkansas runs its elections county by county. The county clerk keeps the voter rolls and handles absentee ballots; the county board of election commissioners runs the polls.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state, and county offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: The usual deadline is 30 days before the election. This year that fell on a Sunday, so it moved to Monday, Oct. 5. Arkansas has no online registration; a mailed form had to be postmarked by this date.

src.label: Arkansas Secretary of State, 2026 election calendar

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: 8 am to 6 pm Monday through Friday, 10 am to 4 pm Saturday. The last day, Monday, Nov. 2, ends at 5 pm. Vote at any early-voting site in your county.

dates.label: Absentee application due (by mail, email, or fax)
dates.detail: Due by 5 pm. Arkansas absentee voting needs a reason allowed by law, such as being away from the county or unable to get to the polls. Applying in person at the clerk's office runs a little later — ask your county clerk.

src.label: Arkansas Secretary of State, 2026 election calendar

dates.label: Absentee ballot hand-delivered by you: last day
dates.detail: If you carry your own absentee ballot to the county clerk, it must be there by close of business the Friday before the election.

dates.label: Election Day — and mailed absentee ballots must arrive
dates.detail: Polls are open 7:30 am to 7:30 pm. A mailed absentee ballot must reach the county clerk by 7:30 pm — a postmark is not enough.

src.label: Arkansas Secretary of State, 2026 election calendar

dates.label: Provisional ballot: show your ID by noon
dates.detail: If you voted a provisional ballot because you didn't have photo ID, show it to the county clerk or election commission by noon on the Monday after the election so your vote counts.

src.label: Washington County Election Commission — voter ID

dates.label: General runoff (only where a race needs one)
dates.detail: Held only in races where no one won outright under Arkansas law.

src.label: Arkansas Secretary of State, 2026 election calendar

id_rule.text: Bring a photo ID issued by the United States, the State of Arkansas, or an accredited Arkansas college — a driver's license, passport, or military ID, for example. It can be expired up to four years. If you have none, your county clerk can issue a free voter verification card. Without ID you can still vote a provisional ballot.
